markets.question: Champions League winner
markets.note: Market favorite: DraftKings has PSG at +500 (captured 31 Aug 2026), clear of a four-way knot at +600 (Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Arsenal) and Real Madrid at +650. PSG are the two-time defending champion and the shortest price on the board, so this is a straight market read rather than a hunch. Worth flagging the market and the leading model disagree here: Opta's supercomputer (10,000 simulations) has Arsenal top at 20.9% and Bayern second at 19.4%, with PSG only fifth at 7.1% behind Man City too — the model thinks the market is overrating a two-time-in-a-row winner's chances of a three-peat. Going with the market as the system's default; confidence held to 3 (not higher) precisely because of that disagreement.

markets.question: Top 8 (direct to round of 16)
markets.note: The eight shortest-priced clubs on the DraftKings winner market (PSG +500 through Manchester United +2000), used as a proxy for overall squad strength across the 8-game league phase. Opta's model broadly agrees on the top of this list (Man City given 86.9% to reach the last 16, Arsenal 93.8% to progress) but rates Liverpool's chances of a deep run higher than the market does and is cooler on Manchester United; kept United in on market pricing since a top-8 pick set is inherently noisy across 36 teams and 8 slots.

markets.question: Champions League top scorer
markets.note: Consensus favorite across books: BetJets has him at 4.50, bet365 at 7/2, both clear of Harry Kane (8.00 / 7/1) and Erling Haaland (9.00). Mbappé is the reigning Champions League top scorer, having scored 15 in 11 appearances last season including a competition-record 13 in the league phase alone, so the market price matches recent, repeated form rather than reputation alone.

markets.question: The two finalists
markets.note: PSG as the outright market favorite (+500) is the straightforward pick. For the second finalist, going with Arsenal over the co-priced Bayern Munich/Barcelona (all +600): Arsenal is Opta's single highest-rated team to win the whole thing (20.9%, ahead of Bayern's 19.4%), which as a proxy suggests the model likes their route to the final specifically, not just their overall squad. Confidence is low (2) because picking 2 exact finalists from a 36-team field eight-plus months out is inherently a low-hit-rate market regardless of read quality.

markets.question: The four semi-finalists
markets.note: Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint Germain and Barcelona are the four highest-rated clubs on a blend of the DraftKings winner board, Kalshi implied probabilities and Opta's 10,000-simulation model. Arsenal is the one pick all three sources agree on: DraftKings +600, Kalshi 20%, and Opta's outright leader at 20.9%. PSG and Barcelona are market-led picks the leading model actively dislikes — Opta has PSG only fifth at 7.1% despite PSG being the +500 outright favourite, and Barcelona at 8.2% — taken here on market-first doctrine rather than model conviction, with Manchester City (Opta 12.3%) and Real Madrid (the biggest market/model divergence: Kalshi 16% vs Opta 4.4%) named as the live alternatives. Honesty note: this is a low-hit-rate market — each pick is roughly a 40% shot to reach the semis, so the realistic expectation is about 1.6 of 4 correct, and all four landing together is only a ~3% event.

markets.question: Dark horse — a club outside the favourites that over-performs
markets.note: Napoli sit well outside the market's outright top tier (not among the DraftKings top 11 favorites found in research) despite entering as reigning Serie A champions with a squad built for a deep continental run. Uncertainty flagged: this pick is a qualitative read on squad quality relative to price rather than a specific researched outright quote for Napoli, since the sources checked did not surface their exact winner odds.
